_readme: THE SERVED CONFIG VALUES — [pipeline 4]B-2, Private/requirements/ (was pipeline/04-backend-platform.md, folded into the JSON spec 2026-08-15)
WHAT THIS FILE IS NOT: it is NOT the list of apps this Worker serves. That set comes from
catalog/apps.json — the catalogue the STAMP already writes (post_gen.dart
_appendToAppsJson, SHOW-1). An app absent from `apps` below is still SERVED; it simply resolves to
`defaults` in full. Adding a key here for an app that is not in the catalogue serves nobody, and
tooling/ci/assert-config-registry.mjs fails on exactly that, because dead data that reads as
configuration is worse than no data.
WHY THE VALUES ARE DATA AND NOT A TS LITERAL. Until 2026-08-07 they were an object literal
`DEFAULT_CONFIGS` in src/config.ts keyed by app id, so `GET /config/lingo` answered 404
`unknown_app` for a content pack that has existed in this repo since the pipeline shipped —
onboarding app #2 meant editing and redeploying the shared Worker, which is the per-app manual step
this factory exists to abolish. A deploy is still required for a catalogue change to reach the
edge (the Worker bundles both files at build time); what is gone is the SOURCE EDIT.
TWELVE READERS, named by file and SYMBOL (never by line: every line number here went stale) — all read STRUCTURE:
· tooling/catalog/render-rail-prices.mjs `REGISTER` — `prices` → services/platform/src/routes/rail-price-ids.ts, the store column's rule, the owner's store sheet
· services/platform/src/config.ts, the `import` of this file — builds the served registry from catalogue x this file
· tooling/ci/assert-config-registry.mjs `DATA` — every key here names a catalogue app, and every served feature has a reader
· tooling/ci/assert-no-store-bundle-copy.mjs `SERVED_COPY` — served copy promises no bundle while none can be bought (G6)
· tooling/ci/assert-purchase-path.mjs `SERVER_CONFIG` — [5]M-8/T-11, every offering's term + trial
· tooling/ci/assert-stamp-properties.mjs `PLATFORM_CONFIG_DATA` — [10]D-8, every served `update_url`, per channel; and every per-channel map's keys
· tooling/sites/generate-discovery.mjs `RAIL_CONFIG` — `features` → the landing page's bullets; `paywall` → its prices
· tooling/sites/generate-landing-payload.mjs `RAIL_CONFIG` (in `REQUIRED_SOURCES`) — the landing payload's prices
· tooling/ci/assert-discovery-surface.mjs `RAIL_CONFIG` — re-parses this file and re-derives those prices
· tooling/ci/assert-render-payload.mjs `RAIL_CONFIG` — own price arithmetic, one currency per app, no price in prose
· tooling/ci/assert-ads-declarations.mjs, pointed here by the android-play ads-declaration.json `configPayloads`
· tooling/ci/release-manifest.mjs `releaseFloor` — the release record's minSupported is the highest `min_supported_version` served to the channels it stages
⏱ 2026-10-01 · EXM-01, EXM-04 (train P47): AN `apps` KEY MAY NAME AN EXTENSION, AND THEN IT CARRIES `paywall` ALONE.
FullShot Pro's tier is recorded here as data: `apps.fullshot.paywall.offerings` is ADR 093's single-app web tier
(the monthly and yearly figures subscriptiontracker's served offerings carry; no lifetime, and no trial while no
renewal notice exists for it), and `prices.apps.fullshot` holds its rails, with no store column because no browser
store sells an in-extension product. An extension is SOLD, never SERVED: services/platform/src/config.ts
`buildExtensionPaywalls` reads that `paywall` for POST /v1/checkout, and no GET /config/<extension> exists. Four more
readers take it from here: extensions/scripts/render-listing.mjs (whether the tool sells, and the Edge price range),
contracts/legal/pro-gate.mjs (whether the privacy page's purchase paragraph is published), tooling/sites/
generate-discovery.mjs (the /pricing section) and tooling/ci/assert-no-price-literals.mjs (the one range the Edge
listing may carry). assert-config-registry.mjs limb 3 refuses any other key on an extension's entry.
🔴 THAT LINE SAID "THREE READERS" UNTIL 2026-08-21 AND "EIGHT" UNTIL 2026-09-22, AND BOTH UNDERCOUNTS
COST AN INVESTIGATION. A reader who trusted the first concluded `apps.subscriptiontracker.features` was
dead data — every `.feature(` call in Dart and every read in the TypeScript tests really does miss it —
and the next step after that conclusion is deleting the keys. On 2026-09-22 the eight also cited every
reader by a line number, and each number had moved. The list is kept because the list was what was
wrong, not the idea of one; it names symbols now, because a symbol moves with its code.
WHY `apps.subscriptiontracker.features` IS NOT DEAD, since the Dart evidence says it should be. Measured 2026-08-21
across 185 non-test Dart files: ZERO of them read `renewals`, `budgets` or `exports`. The only
`.feature(` call in shipped Dart is apps/subscriptiontracker/lib/features/home/home_screen.dart:1573, and it asks
for `promo_card_enabled` — a key this file does not serve at all. The three keys are read on the OTHER
surface: tooling/sites/generate-discovery.mjs FEATURE_NAMES:183-187 maps each one to a reader-facing
title and blurb, and those three bullets are on the live landing page today —
sites/nikatru/apps/subscriptiontracker.html:142-144, served by Cloudflare Pages out of this repo. Setting any of the
three to `false`, or removing it, silently empties a section of a page a stranger reads. A config key
is dead when NOTHING reads it, and "nothing in the language I grepped" is not that.
The rule is now enforced instead of narrated: assert-config-registry.mjs limb 8 unions the Dart
readers and generate-discovery.mjs's FEATURE_NAMES, and fails on a served feature key that is `true`
with no reader in either. A key served `false` with no reader is PRINTED, not failed — that is
`max_promos_per_week`'s shape one field over: a lever that ships disarmed, declared before its reader.
🔴 THE OFFERINGS BELOW ARE THE WEB COLUMN OF ADR 093 §2, AND THIS FILE STATES NO FIGURE IN PROSE.
The decision: Private decisions/093-the-final-prices-the-upi-charge-changes-nothing-in-india-and-the-
dollar-web-prices-are-set.md — §2 sets the prices, §5 leaves the trial length as it stood. Each
`amount_minor` below is the web column's figure for its plan, and the one-time offering carries no trial:
a trial delays the first renewal, and that offering never renews. Until 2026-09-22 this paragraph
restated the prices beside a unit-economics rationale, and the paragraph after it restated a regional
price the owner had since changed. Nothing read either copy, so nothing noticed. A price written in
prose is a second copy of it; assert-render-payload.mjs limb K now refuses any string in this file that
carries a currency sign or code beside a digit, and limb L refuses a trial on a term that never renews.
⬜ ADR 093 ALSO SETS WEB PRICES FOR INDIA, AND NONE OF THEM IS SERVED HERE. That is structural, not an
omission, and two things have to exist before a rupee offering can land in `offerings`:
1. THIS DOCUMENT HAS NO REGION DIMENSION. `offerings` is one flat list per app, every reader renders
all of it to every visitor, and the landing payload carries one `zeroAmount` and one currency line.
A rupee row would print rupee and dollar plans side by side on one public page with no geography.
assert-render-payload.mjs limb J refuses a second currency in one app's list for exactly that reason.
2. NO RAIL HERE TAKES A RUPEE ON THE WEB. India's web and direct buyers pay through Razorpay by owner
decision, and services/platform/src/lib/mor/razorpay.ts verifies a webhook signature but its parse
refuses every event: there is no Razorpay checkout route, no plan id and no webhook secret.
checkout.ts sells the dollar offerings below through Paddle, and nothing else.
The fix is a region-keyed price book: each book one currency and one rail, rendered as its own page and
re-derived by the render and discovery guards with their own arithmetic. Putting rupees here before it
exists would be a price nothing can charge, on a page nobody in India should be shown by default. The
decision lives in the ADR; this paragraph is the pointer, and the open work is row O-WEB-INR-PRICE-BOOK
in Private platform-state/, which closes when the India book is generated, linked both ways with
hreflang, re-derived by both guards, and its buy action reaches a Razorpay route charging those amounts.
🔴 `min_supported_version` AND `update_url` ARE KEYED BY CHANNEL (O-UPDATE-FLOOR-HAS-NO-CHANNEL). Each is a
map from a channel id in tooling/channel-register.json to that channel's value, and `default` answers every
channel the map does not name. A client asks `GET /config/<app>?channel=<its RELEASE_CHANNEL>` and is served
ONE value per field — the wire is scalar, so no client parses a map. No `?channel=` is served `default`; an
id the register does not declare is a 400. An app's own map merges key-wise over the one in `defaults`, and
a scalar anywhere (here, per app, or in a KV override) replaces the map and means every channel. So raising
the floor for `web` alone is one key, `"web": "<version>"`, and it walls no store build. Keys are refused
by assert-stamp-properties.mjs unless they are `default` or a channel id, and every merged map must carry
`default`. The release record's minSupported is the highest floor served to the channels that release
stages (release-manifest.mjs `releaseFloor`).
⏱ 2026-09-29 · train ST-D9: `paywall.pro_features`, `paywall.free_features` and `paywall.trial_copy` are what
the in-app paywall PITCHES, served so a pitch change is a config edit and not a release. The two lists are
feature CODES, never copy: the app resolves each through its own catalogue and draws nothing for a code it has
no words for (apps/subscriptiontracker/lib/state/money_providers.dart `paywallPitchProvider`). The lead's
ruling D-11 sets them: sync is FREE (sign-in is mandatory), Pro is plan and save. `trial_copy` is ruling D-25:
⏱ 2026-10-01 · MO-07: the Pro codes name only what Pro DELIVERS today (ADR 101): `forecast` (the 12-month
forecast) and `caps` (category caps). `plan`/`save` named a pitch, and `save` ("Find savings") gated nothing.
A code joins this list in the PR that ships the feature it names.
no trial is worded in the app until a store trial is configured, so it is served false while `trial_days`
above still describes the web offering. None of the three is a price, and none may become one.
THE PRICE BOOK: what each served offering costs on each STORE and what each RAIL sells it under (O-RAIL-PRICE-IDS-HAND-KEPT).
NOT SERVED, WITH ONE FIELD EXCEPTED. services/platform/src/config.ts reads `sharedApiBaseUrl`, `defaults` and `apps`, and
from this section `webInrMinor` alone (O-WEB-INR-PRICE-BOOK, 2026-10-01): `GET /config/<app>?market=IN`, the buyer's
own declaration and never cf.country, serves each offering at its India web price in INR (config.ts `priceForMarket`).
No KV override sees or moves this section. The web price every other buyer is shown stays `amount_minor` in
`apps.<id>.paywall.offerings`; an entry here is keyed by that offering's `product_id` and adds only what the served
wire does not carry: the plan, the India web price, the store column and the rail handles.
`apps.<id>.<product_id>`: `plan` (single-monthly | single-yearly | single-lifetime, the same enum as app.yaml
`billing.mobileIap.storeProducts[].plan`), `webInrMinor` (ADR 078's India web price, unchanged by ADR 093; ABSENT on a
one-time offering until the Razorpay order path exists, so India buyers are never shown a plan the India rail cannot
sell: render-rail-prices.mjs limb J, PR #1149 ruling item 5), `store`
(ADR 093 section 2's store column: `USD`, `INR` and `readBack`, absent on the lifetime plan, which no store sells) and
`readBack.<apple|google>` is null until that store's console accepts the price, then `{USD, INR, readAt}` as read there;
render-rail-prices.mjs limb H refuses a null one for a plan apps/<id>/app.yaml declares live on that store.
`rails` (`paddle`, `razorpay`: each either a READ-BACK `{priceId|planId, amountMinor, readAt}` or `{pending: <reason>}`).
`bundles.<plan>`: the same shape for a bundle plan (ADR 093 prices the bundle per plan), priced by its own web column; its rail handles
stay in catalog/bundles.json `priceIds`, their one home, and are not repeated here.
RENDERED. tooling/catalog/render-rail-prices.mjs turns `rails` into services/platform/src/routes/rail-price-ids.ts,
which checkout.ts imports; its --check fails on a hand edit to that file. It also grades the store column by ADR 093
section 2's snapping rule (the store price is at least the web price x 1.20, and a store's read-back is never below
it) and prints the owner's store sheet: `render-rail-prices.mjs --store-sheet <app>`.
A rail value is a VENDOR READ-BACK, never typed to match a price above: a rail id and its amount move only after a
read of the vendor's own catalogue, and `readAt` says when. Razorpay is `pending` on every plan until Razorpay PR B
(designed, not briefed) and the owner's plans exist; PR B then reads RAZORPAY_PLAN_IDS from the rendered file.
WHAT A SALE NETS is not written here or anywhere as prose: `render-rail-prices.mjs --net-sheet` derives it per plan and per
channel from this section and tooling/catalog/fee-register.json (each vendor's published fee, read and dated), and every
--check run fails a channel that can sell and nets below the web row of the same plan.
TAX MODE (O-TAX-TREATMENT-STATED-TWO-WAYS, ADR draft tax-mode-per-rail): every rail entry, a read-back or pending, carries
`taxMode`, whether the price it sells already includes the tax due on it: `inclusive`, `exclusive`, or `unread`. `unread`
is allowed only where the mode is a VENDOR READ-BACK nobody has recorded yet: Paddle reports it on the same read that
fetches the price (`GET /prices/<id>` `tax_mode`; `account_setting` resolves through the account tax setting), and the
2026-09-22 and 2026-09-26 reads did not record it, so the next read writes it beside `amountMinor` and `readAt`. Razorpay
is `inclusive` by ADR 093 (Nikatru is the GST seller on that rail and the INR web price includes GST). Every entry of one
rail states the same mode, because the buyer reads ONE tax sentence per rail: tooling/sites/generate-discovery.mjs
renders it into pricing.html, the product page and terms section 4 from this field, and render-rail-prices.mjs limb I
refuses a rail entry with no `taxMode`, a value outside the three, `unread` on a rail whose mode is decided rather than
read (razorpay), and two modes on one rail.
